On another instance indexes shift and the month name/format may differ or the cell may need scrolling, so look it up by description (falling back to the day text) and fail loudly if absent.

          "July", "August", "September", "October", "November", "December"]

steps.analysis: The click opens the time-picker dialog by tapping the start-time field, identified only by its HH:MM text — the literal '18:00' is instance-specific (it's the default/seed time, not the target hour from binding). On another instance the time value, element index, and even the number of HH:MM fields (start + end) differ, so we must regex-match a clickable time TextView and take the first one (start time precedes end time in the list); failure occurs if no time field is rendered (e.g., All-day checked or 12-hour AM/PM format).
steps.snippet:
import re

elems = device.elements()
time_re = re.compile(r"^\d{1,2}:\d{2}$")
matches = [
    (i, e) for i, e in enumerate(elems)
    if e.get("clickable") and time_re.match((e.get("text") or "").strip())
]
if not matches:
    raise LookupError("No clickable start-time TextView (HH:MM) found on EventActivity")
# first HH:MM field in list order is the event start time (end time comes after)
device.click(matches[0][0])

steps.analysis: The click targets the time picker's current-minutes selector (the View showing e.g. '0 minutes') to switch the picker from the hours list to the minutes list. It can fail on other instances because the index differs and the minutes value/description may not be '0 minutes'; the selector is distinguishable from the hour/minute list items by being a clickable View (not a TextView) whose description contains 'minutes'.
steps.snippet:
idx = None
for i, e in enumerate(device.elements()):
    desc = str(e.get('description', ''))
    if (e.get('clickable') and e.get('class_name') == 'View'
            and 'minutes' in desc and 'hours' not in desc):
        idx = i
        break
if idx is None:
    raise RuntimeError('Time-picker minutes selector not found on screen')
device.click(idx)

steps.analysis: The action selects the event-duration option whose label is "{duration_mins} minutes" in the duration picker; it depends only on that description/text, not the index. mins = binding["duration_mins"]
label = f"{mins} minutes"
idx = device.find(description=label, text=str(mins), clickable=True)
if idx is None:

    device.settle(1)
    idx = device.find(description=label, text=str(mins), clickable=True)
if idx is None:
    raise LookupError(f"Duration option '{label}' not found on duration picker")
device.click(idx)
